doc.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015

title: Playing NER Blues from Bridging the Gap
summary: Monk plays an improvised track and they discuss the title and a live St. Louis Blues.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well speaking of being on the road I know you have to be on the road soon. I just wanted to play — let’s see what was I going to play here? I was going to play here? I was going to play —
Oh, the Basie. That’s completely improvised. We just said roll the tape and we followed Rossano. Completely improvised.
And so that was my concept of — well we’ll let it play. That’s that dynamic thing you were talking about. And nobody does that better than Rossano.
I told him yesterday, oh I know what it was, one of the recordings was “St. Louis Blues” you had done.
Oh yeah, that’s on a live record.
Yeah. And there’s one point where he sounds like he’s the horn section of the Basie band. He’s playing [scats].
